newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-AUSTRALIANS NORMAN AND LONARD SHARE EARLY LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-AUSTRALIANS NORMAN AND LONARD SHARE EARLY LEAD.

text.p: Twice winner Greg Norman and his unheralded fellow Australian Peter Lonard shared the lead after nine holes of the British Open on Thursday.
They were deadlocked at four-under-par after the downwind outward half of Royal Troon.
Americans Payne Stewart and Fred Couples caught the two Australians to make a four-way tie for the lead, but they had not completed the front nine.
Norman, champion in 1986 and 1993, birdied the third and fourth holes, dropped a shot at the fifth but then collected further birdies at the sixth, seventh and ninth.
Lonard, a Sydney player celebrating his 30th birthday with a fine round, birdied the first, fourth, sixth and eighth.
While some players were making light of the favourable wind, conditions were not easy and the paramount problem was how to play the approach shots.

The players had the choice of flying them on to the green and hoping they stopped or the riskier option of landing them short and letting them roll on. That left them at the mercy of Troon's capricious bounces.

Local hero Colin Montgomerie, the world number four and like Norman one of the favourites, bounded through the first green but salvaged par after a good chip and finished at the back of the second and third greens, two-putting for par each time.
He birdied the long fourth and sixth holes but dropped shots at the next three holes to turn one-over.
Five times champion Tom Watson, playing with Montgomerie, birdied the first from 20 feet and stood three-under after collecting more birdies at the fourth and sixth.
Mark Calcavecchia, 1989 winner at Troon, was also three-under.
Favourite Tiger Woods was due off at 1205 GMT.
